--arg.Name: --arg
--arg.description: This option passes a value to the jq program as a predefined variable

--argjson.Name: --argjson
--argjson.description: This option passes a JSON-encoded value to the jq program as a predefined variable

--args.Name: --args
--args.description: Remaining arguments are positional string arguments. These are available to the jq program as $ARGS.positional[]

--ascii-output.Name: --ascii-output
--ascii-output.description: Jq usually outputs non-ASCII Unicode codepoints as UTF-8, even if the input specified them as escape sequences

--color-output.Name: --color-output
--color-output.description: By default, jq outputs colored JSON if writing to a terminal. You can force it to produce color even if writing to a pipe or a file using -C

--compact-output.Name: --compact-output
--compact-output.description: By default, jq pretty-prints JSON output. Using this option will result in more compact output by instead putting each JSON object on a single line

--exit-status.Name: --exit-status
--exit-status.description: Sets the exit status of jq to 0 if the last output values was neither false nor null, 1 if the last output value was either false or null, or 4 if no valid result was ever produced

--from-file.Name: --from-file
--from-file.description: Read filter from the file rather than from a command line

--indent.Name: --indent
--indent.description: Use the given number of spaces for indentation

--join-output.Name: --join-output
--join-output.description: Like -r but jq won't print a newline after each output

--jsonargs.Name: --jsonargs
--jsonargs.description: Remaining arguments are positional JSON text arguments. These are available to the jq program as $ARGS.positional[]

--null-input.Name: --null-input
--null-input.description: Don't read any input at all! Instead, the filter is run once using null as the input

--raw-input.Name: --raw-input
--raw-input.description: Don't parse the input as JSON. Instead, each line of text is passed to the filter as a string

--raw-output.Name: --raw-output
--raw-output.description: If the filter's result is a string then it will be written directly to standard output rather than being formatted as a JSON string with quotes

--rawfile.Name: --rawfile
--rawfile.description: This option reads in the named file and binds its contents to the given global variable

--run-tests.Name: --run-tests
--run-tests.description: Runs the tests in the given file or standard input. This must be the last option given and does not honor all preceding options

--seq.Name: --seq
--seq.description: Use the application/json-seq MIME type scheme for separating JSON texts in jq's input and output

--slurp.Name: --slurp
--slurp.description: Instead of running the filter for each JSON object in the input, read the entire input stream into a large array and run the filter just once

--slurpfile.Name: --slurpfile
--slurpfile.description: This option reads all the JSON texts in the named file and binds an array of the parsed JSON values to the given global variable

--sort-keys.Name: --sort-keys
--sort-keys.description: Output the fields of each object with the keys in sorted orde

--stream.Name: --stream
--stream.description: Parse the input in streaming fashion, outputting arrays of path and leaf values

--tab.Name: --tab
--tab.description: Use a tab for each indentation level instead of two spaces

--unbuffered.Name: --unbuffered
--unbuffered.description: Flush the output after each JSON object is printed

--version.Name: --version
--version.description: Output the jq version and exit with zero
